rawRetro.summary: Repair 2 built the after-sales application the previous round left out and fixed the browser-visible defects from the QA feedback. The working tree now carries the full business slice: service collections migration, service desk (services, routes, providers), role/record scoping, workflow auto-accept, scheduler targets, notifications, attachments, external API-key integration, business pages with navigation and zh/en text, and the AI service-assistant surface. Root causes fixed this round: the app was the blank default template (no business pages/routes/routes/providers/seeds); GET /api/customers:list returned SPA HTML because the resource-alias router installed a catch-all use('*') that answered unknown API GET paths; the source-managed auto-accept workflow never executed because its revision was never materialized, so trigger reported skipped/not-found; client route page authz ids (dashboard/customers/...) did not match the seeded service-* grants, which would deny every non-admin; the AI service-assistant had no client surface; and the observer role reached the state machine before the role check, returning 409 instead of 403. Real AI Q&A/retrieval remains legitimately blocked: zero LLM services and no LOCAL vector database, so the AI Knowledge Base page is integrated and reachable but shows its real empty/unconfigured state, and the assistant shows its modeled readiness message instead of fabricating answers. Verified with pnpm typecheck (all three configs), eslint and prettier on the changed files, pnpm test (41 files / 307 tests), a full pnpm build, and an end-to-end dev run on :14000 (alias JSON, workflow runs, schedule list, in-app inbox, role denials, AI employee list).

blockers.title: Typecheck failed: RepositoryPolicy generic drift and dangling service-token imports
blockers.symptom: pnpm typecheck exited 2 with two findings: server/services/repository.ts(51,17) rejected RepositoryPolicy<RepositoryRecord> against RepositoryPolicy<T> at .withPolicy(policy), and server/services/tokens.ts(3-10) could not resolve ./assistant.js, ./dashboard.js, ./devices.js, ./external.js, ./inspections.js, ./knowledge.js, ./manuals.js and ./work-orders.js.
blockers.rootCause: scopedRepository declared its policy parameter as the default RepositoryPolicy (RepositoryRecord) but connection.repository<T>() expects RepositoryPolicy<T>, so the bridge between the authorization policy type and the concrete row type was missing. Separately, the implementation run declared one DI token per business service but never wrote the service modules those type-only imports named, and nothing imported the token module, so the references could never resolve.
blockers.resolution: Kept scopedRepository's public parameter as the general RepositoryPolicy and cast at the withPolicy call (policy as RepositoryPolicy<T>) so the typing seam the module documents stays in one place; the return value was already cast to ScopedRepository<T>. Removed the unreferenced server/services/tokens.ts, which had no importers and named modules that do not exist; reintroduce tokens together with their service contracts when those services are implemented. blockers.rootCause: The provider boot path resolved authorizationToken unconditionally, unlike the sibling providers that guard optional tokens, and the resource alias router's catch-all use('*') middleware intercepted every API path.
blockers.resolution: Guarded ServiceDeskProvider.boot() with container.has(authorizationToken) (matching AIResourcesProvider and ScheduledTasksProvider) and made authorization optional for a minimal host, and removed the alias catch-all as described above. The provider's register() already binds a lazy singleton, so nothing resolves authorization until a caller needs the service. Verified: vitest run tests/logic passes 25 files / 176 tests and the full suite passes 41 files / 307 tests.

blockers.title: Real AI Q&A/retrieval cannot run in this environment
blockers.symptom: The AI Knowledge Base create action fails with 'vectorDatabaseKey is required for LOCAL knowledge bases', no vector database provider other than PGVector is registered, and ai:listLLMServices returns []. There is therefore no embedding service or vector store to process the two Markdown manuals.
blockers.rootCause: The environment provides zero LLM services and no vector database connection, which are prerequisites for knowledge-base vectorization and retrieval. Both are deployment/credential concerns outside the application source.
blockers.resolution: Kept the AI Knowledge Base plugin registered and its page reachable (the QA-observed 404 is gone; the management API returns 200), left the assistant's real readiness state visible, and kept manual work-order handling fully usable. Per the task, real Q&A and retrieval are recorded as blocked/not_run rather than faked with fixed answers. A future environment needs an enabled LLM/embedding service and a vector database before a knowledge base can be created and the manuals processed.

improvements.title: Implementation phase can report completion with an unbuildable tree
improvements.detail: The implementation phase ran for ~2470s and reported status=completed while writing only untracked server scaffolding whose token registry referenced eight modules that were never created. Verification then halted at typecheck, so no later gate (tests, build, browser QA) ever ran.
improvements.suggestedChange: Run the build gate (format, lint, typecheck at minimum) inside the implementation phase before it declares completion, and fail the phase when local imports cannot be resolved.

improvements.title: Repair feedback reached the agent as a raw formatter/typecheck trace
improvements.detail: The only diagnostic supplied was the verify log tail. It identified the two errors correctly, but gave no indication that the rest of the application was missing, leaving the repair agent to reconstruct scope from the working tree.
improvements.suggestedChange: Include a short structural gap summary with the failure feedback (for example, missing route/provider registrations and client pages relative to the requirement) so a bounded repair can distinguish a build break from an entirely absent feature.

improvements.title: QA ran against a commit whose application source was still uncommitted
improvements.detail: All business files were present in the working tree as untracked/modified files while QA executed against the control SHA, so it exercised the blank template and reported defects that the working tree already fixes. The same browser feedback would have been produced even after a correct implementation.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have the verify stage run against the committed repair tree (or fail when the working tree is dirty relative to the SHA under test) so observed failures describe the code actually delivered.

improvements.title: Router-level wildcard middleware is easy to introduce and only fails on unrelated paths
improvements.detail: The alias router used use('*') to attach authentication, which silently turned every unregistered /api GET path into a 401 and only surfaced through an unrelated app-server test. AGENTS.md documents the rule, but nothing automated catches the pattern when it is added.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a lint rule or targeted test that fails when an application route contribution registers a wildcard middleware outside its own prefix, so the leak is caught next to the code that introduces it.
